extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers, policymakers and economists interested in postwar international monetary policy
extracted.subtask_description: News-summary and exposition of Lord Keynes's White Paper proposing an International Clearing Union (the 'bancor' plan) with its objects, institutional features, and policy mechanisms for postwar international currency and credit arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument of international currency
rubrics_metrics.description: An instrument of currency having general acceptability between nations so that blocked balances and bilateral clearings are unnecessary; an instrument of currency used by each nation in its transactions with other nations, operating through whatever national organ (treasury or central bank) is most appropriate, while private individuals, businesses and banks continue to use their own national currency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a primary object: to avoid bilateral blockages and ease multilateral settlements; the union's currency would be used for inter-nation transactions while domestic life uses national monies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderly method for determining relative exchange values
rubrics_metrics.description: We need an orderly and agreed method of determining the relative exchange values of national units, so that unilateral action and competitive exchange depreciations are prevented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan emphasizes preventing competitive devaluations by having agreed procedures to adjust exchange rates rather than unilateral moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate quantum of international currency
rubrics_metrics.description: We need a quantum of international currency which is neither determined unpredictably (e.g., by gold production) nor subject to large variations depending on individual governments' gold policies, but is governed by the actual current requirements of world commerce and is capable of deliberate expansion and contraction to offset deflationary and inflationary tendencies in world demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keynes argues for a supply of international currency (bancor) tied to trade needs and adjustable to stabilize global demand, rather than fixed by gold supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal stabilizing mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: We need a system possessed of an internal stabilizing mechanism by which pressure is exercised on any country whose balance of payments with the rest of the world is departing from equilibrium in either direction, so as to prevent movements which would create for its neighbors an equal but opposite want of balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The union should apply incentives/pressures on surplus or deficit countries to restore equilibrium and avoid spillover effects; later text lists measures (e.g., encouraging currency adjustment or reserve surrender).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed postwar reserve starting plan
rubrics_metrics.description: We need an agreed plan for starting off every country after the war with a stock of reserves appropriate to its import requirements, so that without undue anxiety it can set its house in order during the transitional period to full peacetime conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clearing union should provide or arrange appropriate starting reserves to permit orderly postwar adjustment rather than precipitate restrictive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central technical, non-political institution
rubrics_metrics.description: We need a central institution of a purely technical and non-political character to aid and support other international institutions concerned with planning and regulation of the world's economic life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed International Clearing Union would perform technical settlement and stabilizing functions without being a political authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of reassurance for troubled countries
rubrics_metrics.description: We need a means of reassurance to a troubled world, by which any country whose own affairs are conducted with due prudence is relieved of anxiety, for causes not of its own making, concerning its ability to meet its international liabilities; and which will therefore make unnecessary restrictive and discriminatory methods previously adopted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One object is to remove the pressure that drives countries to protectionism or restrictive measures, by guaranteeing technical support and breathing space during shocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bancor as unit of account: fixed but adjustable in terms of gold
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions between nations operating in the union are to be in terms of a new currency called 'bancor', its value fixed (but not unalterably so) in terms of gold and accepted as the equivalent of gold by all members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bancor is to be the international medium for settlement; its gold-link should be stable but adjustable under agreed procedures; local currencies would be stabilized in terms of bancor with adjustment mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quota system for borrowing and credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each nation would receive fixed quotas as to the amount of borrowing they may do, based on their average trade balances over a period of time; flexible quotas would be given as to the amount of credit they may accumulate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotas are to be calibrated to trade volumes; the White Paper contrasts Keynes's flexible approach with the U.S. proposal (which suggested a $5,000,000,000 fund and different voting arrangements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Management must be genuinely international without veto preponderance
rubrics_metrics.description: Management of the institution must be genuinely international, without preponderant power of veto or enforcement lying with any country or group, and the rights and privileges of smaller countries must be safeguarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keynes warns against any design that gives a single country (e.g., the U.S.) effective veto power; the U.S. plan's voting thresholds (25% American vote, 80% needed for major decisions) are criticized as giving potential veto power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of creditor balances as deposits to fund short-term loans
rubrics_metrics.description: Creditor nations' balances would accumulate as bancor deposits in the union, and the union would lend these deposits for short periods to debtor nations, just as a commercial bank accepts deposits and makes loans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows creditor countries' surpluses to be productively used rather than sterilized as gold hoards, benefiting both creditors (by preserving demand) and debtors (by providing credit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives/measures for excessive debit countries
rubrics_metrics.description: If a country makes excessive use of the fund to accumulate debit balances, the proposal outlines measures to induce the country to improve its position (for example by reducing the value of its currency or surrendering a portion of its gold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The union would apply corrective pressures (including currency adjustment, restraint on domestic credit, or partial gold surrender) to restore balance rather than immediate punitive exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of equality of credits and debits (closed-system banking)
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea is to generalize the banking principle of equality of credits and debits within a closed system: if no credits can be removed outside the clearing system but only transferred within it, the union can never be in difficulty about honoring checks drawn upon it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By keeping transactions internal to the union, its solvency and ability to settle claims is preserved; this is presented as the essential operational principle of the clearing union.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility on gold and capital base (no fixed gold/capital sum)
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan makes no fixed proposal for the amount of gold or capital which the union would have (in contrast to the U.S. Treasury proposal of $5,000,000,000); the union's resources would be governed by trade needs rather than a single fixed sum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keynes's approach subordinated gold rather than eliminating it, allowing gold and other reserves to play a role without being the sole determinant of the union's capacity.
